detail.longDescription: arXiv:2607.18821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An ontology edit can preserve a query answer while replacing the evidence that justified an action on it. We study when the original approval remains valid. VirtualSet compiles the evaluated query and a trusted grant into a single-use capability. The query result fixes the approved objects; policy grants actions on their type. Each field or link is recorded under its owning receiver type. For conjunctive filters over stable, single-valued relations, preserving the observed paths and target rows suffices for current target membership at batch entry. In 32 Java cases requiring recorded evidence, finite paths admitted 24 continuations versus 16 for a type-level closure. We then issued approvals before controlled changes in procurement and laboratory ontologies and presented the original credentials afterward. In all 40 scenarios, the post-change selections returned the same object identifiers as at issuance. With the same Java authorization layer, typed navigation and SQL over a stable view each retained 22 original approvals and blocked 18. Retargeting the second relation invalidated approvals that traversed it while preserving those based only on the first. By tracing the receiver type at each access in a validated query, VirtualSet distinguishes approvals for the same objects according to the evidence each approval depends on.
